evals.prompt: Power for our two-arm RCT of a delirium-prevention bundle: continuous outcome (delirium-free days), assumed d = 0.40 from the method-extract work (range 0.28-0.52), alpha 0.05 two-sided, 80% power, 15% dropout. R project. Need the SAP-6 (sample size and power) paragraph.
evals.expected_output: Picks the two-sample t design, writes a reproducible R script with a sensitivity sweep and plot, captures log/sweep/plot outputs, writes the SAP-ready summary paragraph, and emits the __CE_POWER__ signal.
expectations: Uses pwr::pwr.t.test (two-sample t) and writes analysis/power/<design>-<date>.R with input parameters as a named list
Includes a sensitivity sweep over effect size (covering 0.28-0.52), power, and alpha, saved to analysis/power/<design>-<date>-sweep.csv, plus a plot of N vs effect size
Writes analysis/power/<design>-<date>-summary.md stating alpha, power, effect size source, per-arm and total N, and dropout-inflated enrollment
Cites the effect-size source (the method-extract output and its PMIDs) in the summary and labels the 15% dropout as an assumption rather than a literature value
Emits '__CE_POWER__ design=<name> total=<n> file=<path> n_per_arm=<n> with_dropout=<n>'
Rounds up at every step: 100 per arm, 200 total, 236 enrolled after 15% dropout (ceiling of 200/0.85), and checks the script against the closed-form formula
Does not promise an interim conditional-power look or sample-size re-estimation in the SAP-6 paragraph
Does not install R or Python packages without the user's approval

evals.prompt: Our trial finished with a non-significant result (p=0.12, n=180). The reviewer asked whether we were underpowered - can you compute the observed power from our data?
evals.expected_output: Declines to run post-hoc observed power, explains why it is an anti-pattern, and offers a design-based alternative such as reporting the confidence interval or the detectable effect from the prespecified assumptions.
expectations: Does not compute post-hoc/observed power from the observed effect
Explains that post-hoc power is a statistical anti-pattern
Offers an alternative (e.g. interpreting the CI or a minimum detectable effect under prespecified assumptions)
Does not emit a __CE_POWER__ signal for a post-hoc calculation

evals.prompt: need a sample size for our cohort study on statins and post-op delirium. method-meta-analysis gave me this earlier in the chat: __CE_EFFECT_SIZE__ metric=OR n_studies=6 point=0.72 ci=0.58,0.89 pi=0.41,1.26 i2=48 mode=reml -- use that. we're in python.
evals.expected_output: Stops automatic adoption of the legacy pooled signal until its selected scientific compatibility artifact is supplied and matched to the planned study; does not calculate a misleading sample size.
expectations: Requires the selected compatibility artifact before automatically using a pooled power anchor
Does not fabricate control risk, compatibility metadata or sample size
